Hi Stephanie / Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick demo last week. Peregrine is moving forward with a security review and we need a CAIQ mapping back to your control families plus representative evidence. Two quick asks before we accept the package into our portal:

1) We need an approach for redacting tenant IDs and sample user identifiers from runtime logs. Can you confirm what you can redact and still preserve traceability?
2) We need clarification on scope for three controls where our auditor flagged potential multi-tenant surface: CCM-11 (Data Segregation), CCM-13 (Key Management), and CCM-20 (Logging & Monitoring). Which of those require per-tenant artifacts vs global artifacts?

Timeline: if you can share a draft mapping and redaction plan by EOD Friday (2026-05-22) that would keep us on schedule.

Attachments: none on initial.

Best,

Hi Clara — thanks, and appreciated the clear asks. High level plan below; attaching a draft mapping for your team to review.

Summary plan (high level):
- Redaction: we produce log excerpts with deterministic pseudonyms for tenant/user identifiers and a short key file that maps pseudonym -> original for auditor review only (stored in our secure evidence vault). We will not include full PII in shared artifacts.
- CCM-11 (Data Segregation): provide per-tenant config manifests + architecture diagram (per-tenant). Sample runtime traces will be redacted as above.
- CCM-13 (Key Management): provide global KMS configuration and per-tenant keystore registration records (where applicable). We will produce the key rotation policy and a masked key metadata export.
- CCM-20 (Logging & Monitoring): global logging pipeline diagram + per-tenant retention settings and a redacted sample of alerting records.

Deliverables attached (drafts):
- Peregrine_CAIQ_Mapping_Redacted_v1.xlsx (CAIQ control map + evidence callouts) [attachment: Peregrine_CAIQ_Mapping_Redacted_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 180KB)]
- control_trace_log_snippet.pdf [attachment: control_trace_log_snippet.pdf (pdf, 48KB)]

Next steps / asks for your auditor:
- Confirm whether the auditor requires the pseudonym mapping file (we can make it auditor-access-only via DocuSign NDA / evidence portal).
- If you need full tenant-level logs for an in-person review, we can arrange a sealed session with our compliance team.

Internal notes: tagging Priyom for the log extraction and Kim for the CAIQ crosswalk QA.

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen

Stephanie / Clara — quick technical note from the runtime/logging side:

- For redaction we recommend deterministic hashing with a salt per-evidence-batch. That preserves referential integrity across artifacts while removing raw identifiers. We will store the salt in the evidence vault for auditor retrieval.
- The log extraction will produce a three-file bundle: index.json (metadata), redacted_logs.log (redacted excerpts), and a short trace map.pdf showing which shards / runtime nodes sampled the events. I attached a tiny PDF sample (control_trace_log_snippet.pdf).

Operational constraints: extracting tenant-specific logs requires a short window of elevated read access; we plan to perform the extraction in the staging cluster (non-production copy) unless you explicitly request production traces. Please advise which you prefer.

Owner / timeline:
- Priyom (me) will run the extraction and deliver redacted bundle by 2026-05-22T18:00-07:00 if we target staging.
- Kim will finalize CAIQ mapping QA and produce a clean XLSX the same day.

--
Priyom Das
Platform Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
